newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank raises Lombard rate to 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank raises Lombard rate to 50 pct.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Friday that it was raising its last resort lending facility, the Lombard rate, to 50 percent from a previous 14 percent, effective immediately.
"We are increasing the Lombard rate to 50 percent...with immediate effect," Ludek Niedermeyer, a CNB board member, told Reuters.
He said the move was part of a three-pronged strategy in response to short-selling of the crown.
"At the same time, we will restrict the access of the banks to the Lombard window if necessary and we will adequately change the repo rate in our future open market operations," he said.

The Czech crown has been heavily pressured over the past week as mainly foreign investors pushed the currency lower. The crown hit a record weak point of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market for the first time in over a year.
"We do see some wave of short-selling and the adequate response of the central bank is of course to restrain the liquidity," Niedermeyer said.

"Normally the Lombard rate is not used, but because banks are spending domestic currency and buying foreign currency, there could be a liquidity shortage and in such a circumstance, the central bank is not very happy to provide financing of speculation against the domestic currency," he added.
Niedermeyer also said that the CNB was prepared to raise its repo rate again after a 50 basis point jump to 12.9 percent on Friday, depending on market conditions.
"It will depend on the concrete situation on the money market and forex market on Monday morning," he said.
"We expect that after some wave of short-selling is over, then we will not need extremely high interest rates, but we are ready to use them if the market is volatile," Niedermeyer added.
The crown firmed immediately after Niedermeyer's statement to about -3.3 percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark parity, from -4.19 percent just before he spoke.
